title: Scottish Widows and Aberdeen Allocate UK Workplace Pension Capital to Oxford Quantum Circuits and Quantum Motion via LTAF - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Scottish Widows and Aberdeen made the first deployments from the CG Scottish Widows Growth LTAF, managed by IP Group plc, channeling UK DC pension savings into growth-stage deep tech, with Oxford Quantum Circuits and Quantum Motion anchoring quantum commitments alongside Nyobolt and Genomics Limited.

insights.claim: The CG Scottish Widows Growth LTAF is the vehicle for the first deployments connecting UK defined-contribution retirement assets to venture-stage technology firms, with the mandate managed by IP Group plc.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Opens a new, potentially large and patient capital pool for UK private deep-tech companies, benefiting IP Group.
insights.locator: UK workplace pension provider Scottish Widows

insights.claim: Scottish Widows, part of Lloyds Banking Group, directs roughly 300 billion pounds of assets under administration, and the LTAF is an FCA-authorized structure to hold illiquid private investments within DC pensions.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Even small allocations from a pool this size could be meaningful for UK venture funding.

insights.claim: UK hardware spin-outs needing Series B and follow-on growth capital have historically relied on foreign investment or overseas listings, a gap the LTAF structure is meant to address.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Domestic late-stage capital could reduce pressure on UK quantum firms to redomicile or list abroad.
insights.quote: domestic hardware spin-outs requiring Series B and follow-on growth capital have historically relied on foreign investment or overseas listings

insights.claim: The initial tranche also funds battery developer Nyobolt and genomic medicine firm Genomics Limited alongside the two quantum companies.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Quantum sits in a broader UK strategic deep-tech basket rather than a dedicated quantum allocation.

insights.claim: Oxford Quantum Circuits builds superconducting QPUs using a proprietary 3D coaxial 'Coaxmon' architecture that routes control lines vertically to isolate the qubit plane from cross-talk, deployed in colocation data center racks.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Data-center-ready form factor is part of OQC's commercial positioning.

insights.claim: Quantum Motion develops fault-tolerant silicon spin-qubit processors manufactured in standard 300 mm industrial CMOS foundries.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: CMOS-compatible qubits offer a scaling narrative tied to existing semiconductor manufacturing.

insights.claim: Backing both a superconducting and a silicon spin player reflects a hedge across distinct physical modalities scaling within the UK.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Institutional investors appear to be diversifying modality risk rather than picking a winner.
